_file_header.weight_rule: Weights are DERIVED from evidence_strength and human_evidence (not arbitrary): ESTABLISHED + human evidence = 0.85; ESTABLISHED + no human = 0.70; MODERATE + human = 0.60; MODERATE + no human = 0.45; WEAK = 0.35.
_file_header.pmid_policy: Hallmark links used for scoring must include at least one verified PMID. Links with only unverified PMIDs carry include_in_scoring: false. Unverified PMIDs remain in JSON for manual QA with pmid_verified: false.

Anti-inflammatory signaling in vitro/in vivo models; human translation limited by bioavailability.

hallmark_links.mechanism: mTOR-related modulation and metabolic stress-response biology in experimental senescence models.
Long-term green tea / EGCG exposure in rodent aging studies (verified PMID).
Senescent endothelial context (additional verified PMID in audit list).

Alternate aging-focused review PMID previously used — flagged UNVERIFIED pending manual confirmation.

interactions: Warfarin effect debated — monitor INR if combined.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Fatty acid shuttle into mitochondria; supports beta-oxidation in deficiency states.

dose.context: TMAO microbiome metabolism controversy in CVD risk — context-specific.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Observational and mechanistic links between magnesium status and telomere biology (verified PMIDs).
Magnesium dependence of DNA repair enzymes; deficiency models link to genomic stress (mechanistic).

interactions: Osmotic laxative effect; bisphosphonate absorption spacing.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Taurine supports mitochondrial membrane potential and reduces mitochondrial ROS; taurine deficiency accelerates mitochondrial aging across species.
Taurine supplementation reduces senescence markers (p21, p16) in multiple tissues; plasma taurine declines ~80% from youth to old age.
Taurine modulates mTOR and AMPK signaling pathways in aging tissues.

dose.context: Science 2023 longevity study; 1-6g/day range used in human supplementation trials.

safety_notes: Generally well tolerated; GI upset at high doses.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Urolithin A induces mitophagy, clearing damaged mitochondria and improving mitochondrial quality control in aging muscle.
Mitophagy induction by urolithin A reduces senescent cell burden and SASP in aging tissues.

dose.context: Phase II RCT in older adults; produced by gut microbiome from ellagitannins (pomegranate, walnuts).

safety_notes: Well tolerated in clinical trials; long-term data emerging.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Sulforaphane activates Nrf2/ARE pathway, upregulating DNA repair enzymes and reducing oxidative DNA damage.
Sulforaphane reduces senescence markers via Nrf2 activation and autophagy induction.
Sulforaphane inhibits NF-kB and reduces pro-inflammatory cytokine production.

dose.context: Broccoli sprout extract standardized to sulforaphane content; bioavailability varies by preparation.

interactions: Patients on thyroid medication: MONITOR_THYROID_LEVELS — cruciferous compounds may affect thyroid hormone metabolism.
safety_notes: Generally well tolerated; GI upset possible.
Thyroid medication interaction: monitor thyroid levels.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Melatonin is a potent mitochondrial antioxidant; protects mitochondrial membrane integrity and reduces mitochondrial ROS.
Melatonin modulates circadian epigenetic programs and DNA methylation patterns in aging.
Melatonin reduces oxidative DNA damage and supports DNA repair mechanisms.

dose.context: Lower doses (0.5-1mg) preferred for circadian entrainment; higher doses for antioxidant effects.

interactions: Patients on benzodiazepines or sedatives: ADDITIVE_SEDATION — increased CNS depression risk; clinician review required.
safety_notes: Morning grogginess at higher doses; avoid driving after use.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Zinc is a cofactor for >300 enzymes including DNA repair enzymes; deficiency impairs genomic stability.
Zinc modulates p53 and senescence pathways; zinc deficiency accelerates immunosenescence.
Zinc is essential for immune cell signaling and thymulin production; deficiency impairs immune intercellular communication.

dose.context: Zinc picolinate or gluconate forms preferred; avoid excess (>40mg/day) due to copper depletion.

interactions: High-dose zinc depletes copper — consider copper co-supplementation at doses >25mg/day.
Reduces absorption of fluoroquinolone and tetracycline antibiotics — space by 2 hours.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Selenium is a cofactor for glutathione peroxidases and thioredoxin reductases; deficiency increases oxidative DNA damage.
Selenoproteins protect mitochondria from oxidative damage; selenium deficiency impairs mitochondrial antioxidant defense.

dose.context: Selenomethionine or selenium-enriched yeast preferred; narrow therapeutic window — avoid >400mcg/day.

interactions: Chemotherapy interactions possible — oncology coordination required.
safety_notes: Narrow therapeutic window; selenosis risk above 400mcg/day (hair loss, nail brittleness, neurological symptoms).

hallmark_links.mechanism: Vitamin K2 activates matrix Gla protein (MGP) and osteocalcin, preventing vascular calcification and modulating endocrine signaling.
Vitamin K2 activates SirT1 and reduces senescence markers in vascular cells.

dose.frequency: daily (MK-7 form preferred for longer half-life)
dose.context: MK-7 form has superior bioavailability and longer half-life than MK-4.

interactions: Warfarin/vitamin K antagonists: CONTRAINDICATED or requires close INR monitoring — clinician review mandatory.
safety_notes: Warfarin interaction: vitamin K2 antagonizes anticoagulant effect.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Vitamin C is a potent antioxidant that reduces oxidative DNA damage and supports DNA repair enzyme activity.
Vitamin C reduces oxidative stress-induced senescence and supports collagen synthesis in aging tissues.
Vitamin C modulates immune cell function and reduces inflammatory cytokine production.

dose.context: Liposomal or buffered forms may improve tolerability at higher doses.

interactions: High-dose vitamin C may affect iron absorption — monitor in hemochromatosis.
Oxalate kidney stone risk at very high doses (>2g/day) in susceptible individuals.
safety_notes: GI upset and osmotic diarrhea at high doses.
Oxalate stone risk in susceptible individuals.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Glycine is a methyl donor precursor supporting one-carbon metabolism and DNA methylation balance.
GlyNAC (glycine + NAC) supplementation reduces senescence markers and improves multiple aging hallmarks in older adults.
Glycine supports glutathione synthesis (via GlyNAC); improves mitochondrial function and reduces oxidative stress in aging.

dose.frequency: daily (often combined with NAC as GlyNAC)
dose.context: GlyNAC trials use equimolar glycine and NAC; standalone glycine also studied for sleep and metabolic benefits.

safety_notes: Generally very well tolerated; mild GI effects at high doses.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Pterostilbene activates SIRT1 and modulates DNA methylation patterns; superior bioavailability vs resveratrol.
Pterostilbene activates AMPK and SIRT1, modulating nutrient-sensing pathways in aging models.
Pterostilbene reduces oxidative DNA damage via Nrf2 activation and antioxidant enzyme induction.

dose.context: Better oral bioavailability than resveratrol due to methoxy groups; human longevity trial data limited.

interactions: Anticoagulant caution; CYP2C9 inhibition possible at high doses.
safety_notes: LDL elevation reported at high doses in one human trial — monitor lipids.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Astaxanthin is a potent mitochondrial antioxidant; crosses mitochondrial membranes and reduces mitochondrial ROS.
Astaxanthin reduces oxidative DNA damage and supports DNA repair in human studies.
Astaxanthin reduces inflammatory cytokine production and modulates immune cell signaling.

dose.context: Natural astaxanthin from Haematococcus pluvialis preferred; fat-soluble — take with meals.

safety_notes: Generally well tolerated; skin yellowing (carotenodermia) at very high doses.

hallmark_links.mechanism: PQQ stimulates mitochondrial biogenesis via PGC-1alpha and CREB activation; improves mitochondrial function in aging.
PQQ modulates CREB and NF-kB transcription factors, influencing epigenetic gene expression programs.

dose.context: Often combined with CoQ10 for synergistic mitochondrial support.

safety_notes: Generally well tolerated at recommended doses.

hallmark_links.mechanism: ALA is a mitochondrial cofactor and antioxidant; regenerates other antioxidants (vitamins C, E, glutathione) and improves mitochondrial function.
ALA activates AMPK and improves insulin sensitivity; modulates nutrient-sensing pathways.
ALA reduces oxidative DNA damage via antioxidant network regeneration.

dose.frequency: daily (R-ALA form preferred; take on empty stomach)
dose.context: R-ALA is the biologically active form; racemic ALA also used clinically.

interactions: May enhance insulin/hypoglycemic effects — monitor blood glucose in diabetics.
Thyroid hormone interaction possible — monitor thyroid function.
safety_notes: GI upset common; take with small amount of food if needed.
Hypoglycemia risk in diabetics on medication.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Apigenin inhibits CD38 (NAD+ hydrolase), raising intracellular NAD+ levels and activating sirtuins — epigenetic regulators of aging.
Apigenin activates AMPK and SIRT1 via NAD+ elevation, modulating nutrient-sensing pathways.
Apigenin reduces senescence markers via NAD+/sirtuin axis and anti-inflammatory effects.

dose.context: CD38 inhibitor / NAD+ booster; found in parsley, chamomile; human longevity trial data limited.

interactions: CYP1A2 and CYP2C9 inhibition possible — review concomitant medications.
safety_notes: Generally well tolerated at dietary doses; high-dose supplement data limited.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Acarbose inhibits intestinal alpha-glucosidases, reducing postprandial glucose spikes and modulating nutrient-sensing pathways; ITP longevity data in mice.
Acarbose modulates gut microbiome composition and reduces inflammatory signaling via reduced postprandial glycemia.

dose.context: RUO note: ITP longevity data in mice; FDA-approved for T2DM. Longevity indication not established in humans.

interactions: Patients on insulin: HYPOGLYCEMIA_RISK — acarbose combined with insulin increases hypoglycemia risk; dose adjustment and monitoring required.
Digestive enzyme supplements may reduce efficacy.
safety_notes: GI side effects (flatulence, diarrhea) common — start low and titrate.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Canagliflozin inhibits SGLT2, reducing glucose reabsorption and activating AMPK; ITP longevity data shows lifespan extension in male mice.
SGLT2 inhibition promotes ketogenesis and mitochondrial efficiency; reduces mitochondrial oxidative stress.
SGLT2 inhibitors reduce senescence markers and SASP in cardiovascular and renal tissues.

dose.context: RUO note: ITP longevity data (SGLT2i class); FDA-approved for T2DM, heart failure, CKD. Longevity indication not established.

interactions: Patients on insulin: HYPOGLYCEMIA_RISK — canagliflozin combined with insulin increases hypoglycemia risk; insulin dose reduction may be required.
Diuretics: increased dehydration and hypotension risk.
DKA risk in type 1 diabetes — contraindicated.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Nicotinamide is an NAD+ precursor that supports sirtuin activity and epigenetic regulation of aging genes.
Nicotinamide supports PARP-1 activity for DNA repair; NAD+ is essential for DNA damage response.
NAD+ repletion via nicotinamide improves mitochondrial function and reduces mitochondrial oxidative stress.

dose.context: Distinct from niacin (no flushing); used in skin cancer prevention trials and NAD+ repletion.

interactions: High-dose nicotinamide may inhibit sirtuins at very high concentrations — paradoxical effect at >3g/day.
safety_notes: No flushing unlike niacin; generally well tolerated.
Sirtuin inhibition concern at very high doses (>3g/day).

hallmark_links.mechanism: Lactobacillus supplementation restores gut microbiome diversity and reduces dysbiosis-associated aging phenotypes.
Lactobacillus species modulate gut-immune axis and systemic intercellular signaling via short-chain fatty acids and immune regulation.
Probiotic supplementation reduces systemic inflammatory markers (CRP, IL-6) in aging populations.

dose.context: Multi-strain formulations often preferred; refrigerated storage for viability.

interactions: Immunocompromised patients: use with caution — rare risk of bacteremia/fungemia.
Antibiotics: space by 2+ hours to preserve probiotic viability.
safety_notes: Generally safe; rare serious infections in severely immunocompromised.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Tocotrienols are potent mitochondrial antioxidants; superior to tocopherols in protecting mitochondrial membranes from oxidative damage.
Tocotrienols reduce oxidative DNA damage and support DNA repair mechanisms.

dose.context: Tocotrienol-rich fraction (TRF) from palm or annatto preferred; avoid high-dose alpha-tocopherol which may antagonize tocotrienol absorption.

interactions: Anticoagulants: vitamin E at high doses may enhance anticoagulant effect — monitor INR.
High-dose alpha-tocopherol may reduce tocotrienol absorption.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Akkermansia muciniphila is a keystone gut bacterium; its abundance declines with aging and metabolic disease; supplementation restores gut barrier integrity.
Akkermansia improves insulin sensitivity and metabolic parameters via gut barrier restoration and GLP-1 modulation.
Akkermansia modulates gut-immune axis and reduces systemic inflammatory signaling via improved gut barrier function.

dose.context: Pasteurized (heat-killed) form shown effective in human RCT; live form also studied.

interactions: Immunocompromised patients: use with caution.
Antibiotics: space by 2+ hours.
safety_notes: Well tolerated in human RCT; long-term safety data emerging.

hallmark_links.mechanism: Telomerase activator; cycloastragenol activates TERT expression, potentially slowing telomere attrition.
Telomere maintenance via TERT activation may reduce genomic instability from critically short telomeres.

dose.context: Harley CB et al. Rejuvenation Res 2011; TA-65 is a proprietary cycloastragenol formulation. Evidence is preliminary.

safety_notes: Research Use Only. Not for clinical use.
Autoimmune disease: contraindicated — immune stimulation risk.
Evidence is preliminary; not standard of care.
